summary: Represent process.env as a Node-compatible host environment object rather than a plain Dictionary.

target.notes: Generic property get/set/delete/enumeration must reuse OBJECT/OPERATORS semantics against this specialized runtime object.

semantics.values: environment entries are exposed as strings
semantics.assignment: currently coerces assigned values to strings with Node's documented deprecated implicit conversion behavior
semantics.workers: Worker threads get a copy by default; on Windows Worker copies are case-sensitive
semantics.external_visibility: mutations do not update the parent shell and are not automatically shared with other workers

caveats: Reuse operators.assignment / operators.delete.property rather than inventing separate JavaScript operator semantics.
A Dictionary<string,string> loses undefined-on-missing, JS property behavior, and Windows main-thread case rules.

tests.name: normal set and read through object semantics
tests.expected_behavior: prints "7" because current Node coerces the assigned number to a string
